# Analysis plan: effect of BMI on systolic blood pressure

Two-sample Mendelian randomization with summary statistics. Written before any analysis. All data are simulated.

## Question

What is the causal effect of body mass index (BMI) on systolic blood pressure (SBP), in **mmHg per 1 kg/m² higher BMI**?

## Data

`data/main/exposure_bmi_gwas.tsv` (BMI instruments) and `data/main/outcome_sbp_gwas.tsv` (the same variants looked up
in an SBP GWAS). Column definitions, units and coding are in `data/DATA_DICTIONARY.md`.

## Steps

1. **Read and clean.** Treat the outcome missing-value code as missing. Drop instruments with no usable outcome data.
2. **Harmonise** every variant so that the exposure and outcome effects refer to the same allele (the exposure effect
   allele). Resolve strand differences by complementing alleles. For palindromic variants (A/T or C/G), infer the strand
   from allele frequency when the minor allele frequency is at most 0.42; otherwise drop the variant. Record the
   harmonisation action for every variant.
3. **Units.** Express exposure effects per kg/m² (1 SD of BMI = 4.8 kg/m²).
4. **Estimate.** Primary: inverse-variance weighted (IVW), multiplicative random effects. Sensitivity: MR-Egger
   (report the intercept) and weighted median. Report Cochran's Q for IVW.
5. **Outputs.**
   - `results/harmonisation_log.csv`: one row per variant, with its harmonisation action and whether it was used
   - `results/estimates.csv`: `method, estimate, se, ci_lower, ci_upper, n_snps`
   - `results/figures/scatter.png`: SNP–outcome against SNP–exposure effects, with the fitted lines
   - `report.md`: at most 200 words for the research group
# Data dictionary

> **All data in this folder are SIMULATED** for the IEU AI-for-coding workshop. They describe no real people,
> variants or GWAS. Variant identifiers are synthetic.

## Files

`main/` holds one exposure GWAS file and one outcome GWAS file for the research question.

## `exposure_bmi_gwas.tsv` (exposure: body mass index)

Genetic instruments for BMI from a GWAS of 300,000 people: independent variants (r² < 0.001) associated with BMI at
P < 5×10⁻⁸, pre-selected by the exposure consortium. The exposure consortium does not guarantee which DNA strand
alleles are reported on.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `SNP` | Variant identifier |
| `CHR`, `POS` | Chromosome and position (GRCh38) |
| `EFFECT_ALLELE` | Allele whose effect is reported |
| `OTHER_ALLELE` | Other allele |
| `EAF` | Frequency of `EFFECT_ALLELE` |
| `BETA` | Per-copy effect of `EFFECT_ALLELE` on BMI, in **standard-deviation units** (1 SD of BMI = 4.8 kg/m²) |
| `SE` | Standard error of `BETA` (same units) |
| `P` | P-value |
| `N` | Sample size |

## `outcome_sbp_gwas.tsv` (outcome: systolic blood pressure)

Look-up of the BMI instruments in a separate GWAS of SBP (750,000 people, no sample overlap with the exposure GWAS).
Alleles are reported on the forward strand of GRCh38. Some instruments were not available in the outcome GWAS.
**Missing values are coded as `-9`.**

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rsid` | Variant identifier |
| `chr`, `pos` | Chromosome and position (GRCh38) |
| `A1` | Reference allele |
| `A2` | Alternative allele. **`beta` and `freq` refer to `A2`** |
| `freq` | Frequency of `A2` |
| `beta` | Per-copy effect of `A2` on SBP, in mmHg |
| `se` | Standard error of `beta` |
| `pval` | P-value |
| `n` | Sample size |
# BMI and systolic blood pressure: Mendelian randomization (simulated data)

**Question.** Causal effect of BMI on SBP, in mmHg per 1 kg/m2 higher BMI.

**Data.** 100 BMI instruments; 89 used. Dropped: 4 absent from the outcome GWAS, 3 with missing outcome data, 4 ambiguous palindromic variants (MAF > 0.42). Details: `results/harmonisation_log.csv`. An earlier version mishandled variants whose outcome alleles were complemented and swapped (27 variants); this is corrected, which changed the results.

**Results (mmHg per kg/m2).**
- IVW (random effects): 4.77 (95% CI 3.45 to 6.09)
- Weighted median: 5.20 (95% CI 3.15 to 7.26)
- MR-Egger: 7.33 (95% CI 3.39 to 11.26)

All estimates are positive and all intervals exclude zero. MR-Egger is the least precise and its point estimate is the largest.

**Heterogeneity and pleiotropy.** Cochran's Q = 89.9 on 88 df (p = 0.42): no evidence of heterogeneity. MR-Egger intercept = -0.016 mmHg (95% CI -0.039 to 0.007): no clear directional pleiotropy.

**Caveats.** Results rest on MR assumptions these checks cannot prove. Data are simulated; do not interpret as real findings.
# BMI -> systolic blood pressure: two-sample MR (simulated data)

Implements `analysis_plan.md` in base R. Data dictionary: `data/DATA_DICTIONARY.md`.

## Rerun
From this folder:

    conda run -n ieu-ai-workshop Rscript analysis/mr_analysis.R data/main

(The dataset folder argument is optional; default is `data/main`.) Outputs:
`results/estimates.csv`, `results/harmonisation_log.csv`, `results/figures/scatter.png`.
The script also regenerates a basic `report.md`, overwriting the hand-edited version; the
edited report is the one for the group, so keep a copy before rerunning.

## Test
    conda run -n ieu-ai-workshop Rscript tests/test_known_answer.R

Simulates exposure and outcome files covering every allele situation (aligned, swapped, complemented,
complemented and swapped, palindromic on same/opposite strand, plus dropped cases) with a true effect of
2 mmHg per kg/m2, runs the script and checks the log labels and that IVW, MR-Egger and weighted median recover it.

## Headline result
89 of 100 instruments used. IVW estimate: **4.77 mmHg SBP per 1 kg/m2 BMI (95% CI 3.45 to 6.09)**.
Weighted median 5.20 (3.15 to 7.26); MR-Egger 7.33 (3.39 to 11.26), intercept -0.016 (-0.039 to 0.007).
Cochran's Q = 89.9 (df 88, p = 0.42), so there is no evidence of heterogeneity. The direction is positive in all methods
and all intervals exclude zero. Data are simulated.

Correction: an earlier version did not negate the outcome effect for variants whose outcome alleles are the
complement of the exposure alleles with order swapped (27 variants, now labelled
"strand: complemented and allele order swapped, flipped"). This had biased the IVW estimate towards zero (previously 1.59).

@AGENTS.md
# Notes for AI agents in this project

- All data are simulated. The researcher directs and reviews the work; keep it easy to check.
- Run R as `conda run -n ieu-ai-workshop Rscript <file>`. Base R only: do not install or load add-on packages.
- Analysis code goes in `analysis/`, outputs in `results/`. Use relative paths. Stay inside this folder.
- Quote numbers from the files in `results/`, not from memory.
- Put any scratch or temporary files in `scratch/` inside this folder, not in /tmp.
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# Known-answer test for analysis/mr_analysis.R.
# Simulates exposure/outcome GWAS files (same formats as data/DATA_DICTIONARY.md) with a known
# causal effect, covering every allele situation, runs the analysis script and checks the result.
# Usage (from the project root): Rscript tests/test_known_answer.R
# Work happens in scratch/known_answer/ (removed on success).

THETA <- 2.0      # true causal effect: mmHg SBP per 1 kg/m2 BMI
SD_BMI <- 4.8
set.seed(1)

root <- normalizePath(".")
script <- file.path(root, "analysis", "mr_analysis.R")
stopifnot(file.exists(script))
work <- file.path(root, "scratch", "known_answer")
unlink(work, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(file.path(work, "data"), recursive = TRUE)

comp <- function(a) c(A = "T", T = "A", C = "G", G = "C")[a]
K <- 40   # variants per usable category

# Each usable category: exposure alleles, whether the outcome is on the opposite strand,
# whether outcome A2 is the (strand-equivalent of the) exposure effect allele, EAF range.
cats <- list(
  aligned           = list(pal = FALSE, strand = FALSE, a2_is_ea = TRUE,  eaf = c(.1, .9),
                           expect = "none: alleles aligned"),
  swapped           = list(pal = FALSE, strand = FALSE, a2_is_ea = FALSE, eaf = c(.1, .9),
                           expect = "flipped: allele order swapped"),
  complemented      = list(pal = FALSE, strand = TRUE,  a2_is_ea = TRUE,  eaf = c(.1, .9),
                           expect = "strand: complemented, no flip"),
  complemented_swap = list(pal = FALSE, strand = TRUE,  a2_is_ea = FALSE, eaf = c(.1, .9),
                           expect = "strand: complemented and allele order swapped, flipped"),
  pal_same_ea       = list(pal = TRUE,  strand = FALSE, a2_is_ea = TRUE,  eaf = c(.1, .3),
                           expect = "palindromic: same strand (inferred from EAF), no flip"),
  pal_same_oa       = list(pal = TRUE,  strand = FALSE, a2_is_ea = FALSE, eaf = c(.1, .3),
                           expect = "palindromic: same strand (inferred from EAF), flipped"),
  pal_opp_ea        = list(pal = TRUE,  strand = TRUE,  a2_is_ea = TRUE,  eaf = c(.1, .3),
                           expect = "palindromic: strand flipped (inferred from EAF), no flip"),
  pal_opp_oa        = list(pal = TRUE,  strand = TRUE,  a2_is_ea = FALSE, eaf = c(.1, .3),
                           expect = "palindromic: strand flipped (inferred from EAF), flipped"))

nonpal_pairs <- list(c("A", "C"), c("A", "G"), c("C", "T"), c("G", "T"))
pal_pairs    <- list(c("A", "T"), c("C", "G"))

exp_rows <- list(); out_rows <- list(); truth <- character()
id <- 0
new_id <- function() { id <<- id + 1; sprintf("rs%d", 1000000 + id) }

for (nm in names(cats)) {
  ct <- cats[[nm]]
  for (k in seq_len(K)) {
    snp <- new_id()
    pr <- sample(if (ct$pal) pal_pairs else nonpal_pairs, 1)[[1]]
    if (runif(1) < .5) pr <- rev(pr)
    ea <- pr[1]; oa <- pr[2]
    eaf <- runif(1, ct$eaf[1], ct$eaf[2])
    bx_sd <- sample(c(-1, 1), 1) * runif(1, 0.03, 0.08)         # per SD
    sx <- 0.003
    bx_obs <- bx_sd + rnorm(1, 0, sx)
    sy <- 0.03
    by_ea <- THETA * bx_sd / SD_BMI + rnorm(1, 0, sy)   # true effect of EA on SBP (+noise)
    # outcome representation
    ea_f <- if (ct$strand) unname(comp(ea)) else ea
    oa_f <- if (ct$strand) unname(comp(oa)) else oa
    if (ct$a2_is_ea) { a2 <- ea_f; a1 <- oa_f; b <- by_ea;  f <- eaf }
    else             { a2 <- oa_f; a1 <- ea_f; b <- -by_ea; f <- 1 - eaf }
    exp_rows[[snp]] <- data.frame(SNP = snp, CHR = 1, POS = id * 1000, EFFECT_ALLELE = ea,
      OTHER_ALLELE = oa, EAF = round(eaf, 4), BETA = bx_obs, SE = sx, P = 1e-20, N = 300000)
    out_rows[[snp]] <- data.frame(rsid = snp, chr = 1, pos = id * 1000, A1 = a1, A2 = a2,
      freq = round(f, 4), beta = b, se = sy, pval = 0.1, n = 750000)
    truth[snp] <- ct$expect
  }
}

# Variants that must be dropped
add_drop <- function(label, n, ea, oa, eaf, a1, a2, outfreq = NULL, miss = FALSE, absent = FALSE) {
  for (k in seq_len(n)) {
    snp <- new_id()
    exp_rows[[snp]] <<- data.frame(SNP = snp, CHR = 1, POS = id * 1000, EFFECT_ALLELE = ea,
      OTHER_ALLELE = oa, EAF = eaf, BETA = 0.05, SE = 0.003, P = 1e-20, N = 300000)
    if (!absent) {
      out_rows[[snp]] <<- if (miss)
        data.frame(rsid = snp, chr = -9, pos = -9, A1 = -9, A2 = -9, freq = -9, beta = -9,
                   se = -9, pval = -9, n = -9)
      else data.frame(rsid = snp, chr = 1, pos = id * 1000, A1 = a1, A2 = a2,
                      freq = if (is.null(outfreq)) eaf else outfreq, beta = 5, se = 0.03,
                      pval = 0.1, n = 750000)
    }
    truth[snp] <<- label
  }
}
add_drop("dropped: palindromic, MAF > 0.42 (strand ambiguous)", 4, "A", "T", 0.47, "T", "A")
add_drop("dropped: allele mismatch", 4, "A", "C", 0.3, "A", "G")
add_drop("dropped: outcome data missing (-9)", 4, "A", "C", 0.3, NA, NA, miss = TRUE)
add_drop("dropped: not in outcome GWAS", 4, "A", "C", 0.3, NA, NA, absent = TRUE)
add_drop("dropped: non-ACGT or indel alleles", 2, "A", "C", 0.3, "I", "D")
# the indel rows carry A1/A2 = I/D in the outcome only; exposure alleles are valid

ex <- do.call(rbind, exp_rows); ou <- do.call(rbind, out_rows)
ex <- ex[sample(nrow(ex)), ]; ou <- ou[sample(nrow(ou)), ]
write.table(ex, file.path(work, "data", "exposure_bmi_gwas.tsv"), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
write.table(ou, file.path(work, "data", "outcome_sbp_gwas.tsv"), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

# ---- run the analysis script on the simulated data (cwd = work, so outputs stay in scratch)
rscript <- file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript")
old <- setwd(work)
res <- system2(rscript, c(shQuote(script), "data"), stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE)
setwd(old)
status <- attr(res, "status"); if (is.null(status)) status <- 0
if (status != 0) { cat(res, sep = "\n"); stop("analysis script failed") }

est <- read.csv(file.path(work, "results", "estimates.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
lg  <- read.csv(file.path(work, "results", "harmonisation_log.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

fails <- character()
check <- function(ok, msg) { cat(if (ok) "PASS  " else "FAIL  ", msg, "\n", sep = ""); if (!ok) fails <<- c(fails, msg) }

# 1. harmonisation labels per variant
lg$expected <- truth[lg$SNP]
check(nrow(lg) == length(truth), "one log row per simulated variant")
bad <- lg[lg$harmonisation_action != lg$expected, ]
check(nrow(bad) == 0, sprintf("harmonisation action matches expectation for all variants (%d mismatches)", nrow(bad)))
if (nrow(bad)) print(head(bad[, c("SNP", "harmonisation_action", "expected")]))
check(all(lg$used == !grepl("^dropped", lg$expected)), "used flag matches expectation")

# 2. recovery of the causal effect
n_used <- sum(!grepl("^dropped", truth))
check(all(est$n_snps == n_used), sprintf("n_snps = %d usable variants", n_used))
for (m in c("IVW (multiplicative random effects)", "MR-Egger", "Weighted median")) {
  r <- est[est$method == m, ]
  ok <- THETA >= r$ci_lower && THETA <= r$ci_upper && abs(r$estimate - THETA) < 0.5
  check(ok, sprintf("%s recovers %.1f: %.3f (95%% CI %.3f to %.3f)", m, THETA, r$estimate, r$ci_lower, r$ci_upper))
}
ei <- est[est$method == "MR-Egger intercept", ]
check(ei$ci_lower <= 0 && ei$ci_upper >= 0, "MR-Egger intercept CI includes 0 (no pleiotropy simulated)")

if (length(fails)) stop(length(fails), " check(s) failed")
unlink(work, recursive = TRUE)
cat("All checks passed.\n")

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# Known-answer test for analysis/mr_analysis.R.
# Simulates exposure/outcome GWAS files (same formats as data/DATA_DICTIONARY.md) with a known
# causal effect, covering every allele situation, runs the analysis script and checks the result.
# Usage (from the project root): Rscript tests/test_known_answer.R
# Work happens in scratch/known_answer/ (removed on success).

THETA <- 2.0      # true causal effect: mmHg SBP per 1 kg/m2 BMI
SD_BMI <- 4.8
set.seed(1)

root <- normalizePath(".")
script <- file.path(root, "analysis", "mr_analysis.R")
stopifnot(file.exists(script))
work <- file.path(root, "scratch", "known_answer")
unlink(work, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(file.path(work, "data"), recursive = TRUE)

comp <- function(a) c(A = "T", T = "A", C = "G", G = "C")[a]
K <- 40   # variants per usable category

# Each usable category: exposure alleles, whether the outcome is on the opposite strand,
# whether outcome A2 is the (strand-equivalent of the) exposure effect allele, EAF range.
cats <- list(
  aligned           = list(pal = FALSE, strand = FALSE, a2_is_ea = TRUE,  eaf = c(.1, .9),
                           expect = "none: alleles aligned"),
  swapped           = list(pal = FALSE, strand = FALSE, a2_is_ea = FALSE, eaf = c(.1, .9),
                           expect = "flipped: allele order swapped"),
  complemented      = list(pal = FALSE, strand = TRUE,  a2_is_ea = TRUE,  eaf = c(.1, .9),
                           expect = "strand: complemented, no flip"),
  complemented_swap = list(pal = FALSE, strand = TRUE,  a2_is_ea = FALSE, eaf = c(.1, .9),
                           expect = "strand: complemented and allele order swapped, flipped"),
  pal_same_ea       = list(pal = TRUE,  strand = FALSE, a2_is_ea = TRUE,  eaf = c(.1, .3),
                           expect = "palindromic: same strand (inferred from EAF), no flip"),
  pal_same_oa       = list(pal = TRUE,  strand = FALSE, a2_is_ea = FALSE, eaf = c(.1, .3),
                           expect = "palindromic: same strand (inferred from EAF), flipped"),
  pal_opp_ea        = list(pal = TRUE,  strand = TRUE,  a2_is_ea = TRUE,  eaf = c(.1, .3),
                           expect = "palindromic: strand flipped (inferred from EAF), no flip"),
  pal_opp_oa        = list(pal = TRUE,  strand = TRUE,  a2_is_ea = FALSE, eaf = c(.1, .3),
                           expect = "palindromic: strand flipped (inferred from EAF), flipped"))

nonpal_pairs <- list(c("A", "C"), c("A", "G"), c("C", "T"), c("G", "T"))
pal_pairs    <- list(c("A", "T"), c("C", "G"))

exp_rows <- list(); out_rows <- list(); truth <- character()
id <- 0
new_id <- function() { id <<- id + 1; sprintf("rs%d", 1000000 + id) }

for (nm in names(cats)) {
  ct <- cats[[nm]]
  for (k in seq_len(K)) {
    snp <- new_id()
    pr <- sample(if (ct$pal) pal_pairs else nonpal_pairs, 1)[[1]]
    if (runif(1) < .5) pr <- rev(pr)
    ea <- pr[1]; oa <- pr[2]
    eaf <- runif(1, ct$eaf[1], ct$eaf[2])
    bx_sd <- sample(c(-1, 1), 1) * runif(1, 0.03, 0.08)         # per SD
    sx <- 0.003
    bx_obs <- bx_sd + rnorm(1, 0, sx)
    sy <- 0.03
    by_ea <- THETA * bx_sd / SD_BMI + rnorm(1, 0, sy)   # true effect of EA on SBP (+noise)

    oa_f <- if (ct$strand) unname(comp(oa)) else oa
    if (ct$a2_is_ea) { a2 <- ea_f; a1 <- oa_f; b <- by_ea;  f <- eaf }
    else             { a2 <- oa_f; a1 <- ea_f; b <- -by_ea; f <- 1 - eaf }

  }
}

add_drop <- function(label, n, ea, oa, eaf, a1, a2, outfreq = NULL, miss = FALSE, absent = FALSE) {
  for (k in seq_len(n)) {
    snp <- new_id()
    exp_rows[[snp]] <<- data.frame(SNP = snp, CHR = 1, POS = id * 1000, EFFECT_ALLELE = ea,

                      freq = if (is.null(outfreq)) eaf else outfreq, beta = 5, se = 0.03,

    }
    truth[snp] <<- label
  }

est <- read.csv(file.path(work, "results", "estimates.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
lg  <- read.csv(file.path(work, "results", "harmonisation_log.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

fails <- character()
check <- function(ok, msg) { cat(if (ok) "PASS  " else "FAIL  ", msg, "\n", sep = ""); if (!ok) fails <<- c(fails, msg) }

# 1. harmonisation labels per variant
lg$expected <- truth[lg$SNP]
check(nrow(lg) == length(truth), "one log row per simulated variant")
bad <- lg[lg$harmonisation_action != lg$expected, ]
check(nrow(bad) == 0, sprintf("harmonisation action matches expectation for all variants (%d mismatches)", nrow(bad)))
if (nrow(bad)) print(head(bad[, c("SNP", "harmonisation_action", "expected")]))
check(all(lg$used == !grepl("^dropped", lg$expected)), "used flag matches expectation")

# 2. recovery of the causal effect
n_used <- sum(!grepl("^dropped", truth))
check(all(est$n_snps == n_used), sprintf("n_snps = %d usable variants", n_used))
for (m in c("IVW (multiplicative random effects)", "MR-Egger", "Weighted median")) {
  r <- est[est$method == m, ]

check(ei$ci_lower <= 0 && ei$ci_upper >= 0, "MR-Egger intercept CI includes 0 (no pleiotropy simulated)")

**Verdict:** the IVW number reproduces and I'd release the report with minor revisions. The one thing I'd hold back is the "no pleiotropy" wording. Everything below is from my own code (`scratch/rev.R`, `scratch/rev2.R`). I did not use `analysis/mr_analysis.R`. I did not edit the project or re-run the test.

## 1. Independent IVW recomputation
I read the plan and dictionary, then harmonised from the raw files myself. The outcome `beta` and `freq` refer to **A2**. Exposure `BETA` and `SE` were divided by 4.8 to give kg/m² units.

| Quantity | Mine | Reported |
|---|---|---|
| Variants used | 89 (100 exposure rows, 96 in the outcome file, 3 with `-9`, 4 ambiguous palindromes) | 89 |
| IVW estimate (multiplicative random effects) | 4.7727, SE 0.6732 | 4.7727, SE 0.6732 |
| IVW 95% CI | 3.453 to 6.092 | 3.453 to 6.092 |
| Cochran's Q | 89.94 on 88 df, p = 0.423 | 89.9 on 88 df, p = 0.42 |
| MR-Egger slope | 7.325 (SE 1.98) | 7.325 |
| MR-Egger intercept | −0.0159 (SE 0.0116) | −0.016 |
| Weighted median | 5.203, bootstrap SE 1.06 | 5.20 (CI 3.15 to 7.26) |

- **Pre-fix figure:** leaving the 27 complemented-and-swapped variants un-negated gives 1.587. That matches the "previously 1.59" in the README.
- **Harmonisation log:** my palindrome calls give the same actions as the log (2 same strand, 2 opposite strand, 4 dropped).
- **Input checks:** there are no duplicate IDs. P-values are consistent with beta/SE. The mean first-stage z² is about 85, so the instruments are strong.

## 2. Could the known-answer test share the analysis's mistake?
Yes, for several assumptions.
- **Shared reading of the dictionary.** The test builds the outcome data with beta and freq on A2, and the same unit conversion. If the dictionary had been misread (A1 instead of A2, or ×4.8 instead of ÷4.8), the test and the script would still agree. My code matches the dictionary, so there is no actual error here. But the test cannot detect one.
- **Palindromes are too easy.**
  - Outcome frequencies are exactly the exposure EAF, with no noise, and EAF is confined to 0.1–0.3.
  - In the real data, the inferred strand rests on frequency gaps like 0.1465 versus 0.8506.
  - The 0.42 threshold and near-0.5 cases are untested, apart from one fixed 0.47 case.
- **Label check is circular.** The expected action strings are the script's own labels, so they only prove the script matches itself. Only the effect-recovery checks test sign.
- **Written after the bug.** The test was added once the complemented-and-swapped bug was found. It covers that failure but says nothing about unknown ones.
- **Not covered:** `-9` appearing in only some columns, and duplicate IDs. The README lists "dropped" cases as coverage, but the real data contains none of the mismatch or indel types.

The test does catch a sign error in any one of the 8 categories, because each is 1/8 of the variants and the tolerance is ±0.5. My independent recomputation is the stronger evidence.

## 3. Plausibility of the numbers
- **Magnitude.** 4.77 mmHg per kg/m² is 22.9 mmHg per SD of BMI. That is several times larger than real-world MR estimates of about 1 mmHg per kg/m². The data are simulated and the arithmetic is right, so this is fine as an exercise. It should not be read as a physiological finding.
- **Q.** Q/df ≈ 1.02 is plausible for simulated data.
- **MR-Egger.** The slope (7.3) is well above IVW (4.8), but the intercept CI includes 0 and has little power. The slope CI is wide.
- **Confidence intervals.** IVW and the weighted median use normal critical values, while MR-Egger uses t. This is minor but inconsistent.
- **Subgroup spread.** IVW by harmonisation class ranges from 2.9 (aligned, 19 variants) to about 10 (the four palindromes). Those are noisy small groups and nothing alarming.
- **Scatter plot.** It looks right: positive slope, bars are 95% CIs, and effects are oriented to positive exposure effects.

## 4. Claims: release, revise or withdraw

| Claim | Decision | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 100 instruments, 89 used; drops of 4, 3 and 4 | **Release** | Reproduced exactly. |
| Correction: 27 variants fixed, results changed | **Release** | 27 matches the log, and the pre-fix IVW of 1.59 reproduces. |
| IVW 4.77 (3.45 to 6.09) | **Release** | Exact match. |
| Weighted median 5.20 (3.15 to 7.26) | **Release** | Estimate matches. I only checked that the SE is close (bootstrap 1.06 versus 1.05 reported). |
| MR-Egger 7.33 (3.39 to 11.26); "least precise, largest" | **Release** | Matches. |
| "All positive, all intervals exclude zero" | **Release** | True. |
| Q = 89.9 on 88 df, "no evidence of heterogeneity" | **Release** | Matches. |
| Egger intercept −0.016 (−0.039 to 0.007), "no clear directional pleiotropy" | **Revise** | The number is right, but "no clear pleiotropy" over-reads a low-powered test. Suggested wording: "no evidence of directional pleiotropy, though the test has limited power". |
| Caveats: MR assumptions unproven, simulated data | **Release** | Keep it. I'd add one line that 22.9 mmHg per SD of BMI is far above real-world estimates. |
| `report.md` is at most 200 words | **Release** | It is 174 words. |
| README: test "recovers" the effect and covers "every allele situation" | **Revise** | Say that it shares the script's reading of the dictionary, uses easy palindromes, and was written after the bug. |
| README: rerunning the script overwrites the hand-edited `report.md` | **Revise (hazard)** | The group's report is committed and would be clobbered by a rerun. I'd write the generated report to `results/` instead. |

I'd withdraw nothing. The only open item is the Egger wording above.
